rules.sentence: Basic elements for differential diagnosis between the pyogenic and tuberculous forms of infectious spondylodiscitis.
Symptom duration (onset) 3 months (acute or subacute)
Symptom duration (onset) 7 months (subacute)
Patient history Recent surgery, bacterial infection, immunosuppressed status, or IV access device use
A history of tuberculosis, or symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis (either spinal or extraspinal), and/or residence/visit in a country where tuberculosis is endemic
Signs of sepsis More common
Signs of sepsis Less common
High fever More common
High fever Less common
Spinal deformity Less common
Spinal deformity More common
Markers of inflammation are usually raised
Markers of inflammation may be slightly raised or even normal
X-ray Osteopaenic changes in the subchondral layer; erosive and blurred endplate margins, diminished intervertebral spaces; paravertebral soft tissue mass
X-ray Rarefaction of vertebral end plates, osseous destruction, disc height loss, new bone formation, and soft tissue abscesses, along with gibbous deformity
CT Bone destruction and involvement of paravertebral tissue, along with abscesses or gas inclusions; no gibbous deformity and calcified masses
CT Visualization of the characteristic gibbous deformity and bone destruction; loss of cortical definition; presence of calcified and large paraspinal masses
PET/CT Increased uptake value in the infected region
PET/CT Maximum standardized uptake value is higher if the imaging is not delayed

MRI Less pronounced T2-hypointensity in some patients; involvement of 2 vertebrae is more frequent;lower degree of bone invasion; decreased loss of cortical definition; diffuse and homogenous enhancement pattern; presence of a disc abscess with peridiscal rim is more common

MRI More pronounced T2-hypointensity in some patients;Involvement of 3 vertebrae is more frequent; higher degree of disc preservation; increased loss of cortical definition; focal and heterogenous enhancement pattern; frequent vertebral collapse and spinal deformity; absence of osteosclerosis and rim-like peripheral contrast enhancement with sharp demarcation on T1-weighted images with specific protocols
